title: Hidden Switching Can Increase Record-Assisted Work at Fixed Distinguishability
content: A controller who knows a preparation label can extract work by choosing a different unitary for each label. How much does this gain change if every output preserves a common subspace that can be measured without disturbing it? We compare sources at the same upper bound on optimal single-copy label discrimination. With four qutrit labels and a degenerate excited doublet, switching among four sector-preserving devices with a setting hidden from both controller and observer exceeds the optimum over all fixed-sector sources, including arbitrary label priors, by Δ/144, where Δ is the excitation energy. At degeneracy the switched source leaves a smaller total excited population. Because it retains population in the upper level, the work advantage vanishes at a doublet splitting of Δ/6 and changes sign beyond it. A calibrated target-population measurement identifies a visibility threshold beyond which even independently switched devices cannot reproduce the outputs. For one more label than the dimension and a nondegenerate ground level in dimensions D ≥ 3, switching improves intermediate work at a fixed guessing budget while preserving the threshold for maximal work.
